title: The contact reports as the canon's provenance
statement: The Raelian canon originates in two reported contact events: Claude Vorilhon's reported encounter of December 13, 1973 at the Puy-de-Lassolas crater near Clermont-Ferrand, producing the six-day teaching published as The Book Which Tells the Truth, and the reported second contact of October 7, 1975, producing Extra-Terrestrials Took Me to Their Planet; the reports themselves — as publication history and movement founding — are documented fact, and everything the framework builds stands on these reports as reports.

includes: The report layer, which is documented: the dates, the location, the publication sequence, the founding of the movement around the reports — attested by the published books themselves and the academic histories
The provenance function: the canon's textual basis is these reports; source discipline for every framework claim runs through this fact

The claim-model consequence, stated in the core's own terms: that a source explicitly reports an event establishes the report, not the event — this record is the corpus's standing instance of that rule applied to its own foundation
excludes: The historicity of the reported encounters, which is exactly what this record does not assert; that question belongs to woh-claim-0001 and its evidence discipline
The content of the messages, carried by the claims that cite them
Biographical claims about Vorilhon beyond the report-and-publication history
Any authentication argument from the reports' internal features

alternatives.statement: The messages were composed rather than received; the reports are a literary frame. This alternative contests the encounters, not the reports — which is why the record's scope makes room for it without being touched by it.

revision_triggers: Documentary evidence changes the publication or founding chronology this record states.
Public prose begins citing this record as if it established the encounters rather than the reports, which is the record's one forbidden use.
